description:
FILED s473t5c (#1501 round 4, `comp/` CHECK 2).  PRE-EXISTING.

PCL reads `use 5.NN` for its feature bundles (that part works -- #455) but
never evaluates the version as a REQUIREMENT.  Three spellings, all silently
satisfied:

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, perl v5.40.3):

    eval "use 10.0.2;"   perl  "Perl v10.0.2 required--this is only v5.40.3,
                                stopped at (eval 1) line 1.\nBEGIN failed--..."
                         PCL   $@ empty
    eval "use 6.000;"    perl  "Perl v6.0.0 required--this is only v5.40.3, ..."
                         PCL   $@ empty
    eval "no 5.000;"     perl  "Perls since v5.0.0 too modern--this is v5.40.3, ..."
                         PCL   $@ empty
    eval "use 5.6;"      perl  "Perl v5.600.0 required (did you mean v5.6.0?)
                                --this is only v5.40.3, ..."
                         PCL   $@ empty
    eval "use 5.000;"    perl  $@ empty   PCL $@ empty       (the satisfied case)
  and for a module, with $Foo::VERSION = 1.0 and Foo.pm present, perl compares
  against `$Foo::VERSION` and dies
    "Foo version 1.01 required--this is only version 1.0 at ..."
  while PCL loads and returns.

WHAT IT COSTS: t/comp/use.t DIFF 40/47.  Of its 47 fail rows, **34** are this
one fact -- tests 6, 9, 11-16, 19, 20 (the perl-version half, including the
four `did you mean vX.Y.Z?` rows and the `%.6f`-formatted `$]`+1 forms), 40,
45, 46, 48, 50, 52, 54, 56, 58, 59 (the `use test_use VERSION` half, three
times over for a numeric, a string and a v-string `$VERSION`) and 69, 71, 84,
86 (`no N.N` / `use vN.N.N`).  The other 13: 9 rows are strict enforcement
(NS:`use strict 'refs'` is not enforced ... / the strict subs+vars siblings)
and 4 are `use 5.39.0` not importing `builtin`'s `true`/`false`.

SIZE / WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A COMPARISON: the four message templates are
part of the assertion (every row is a `like`), so the USER ruling "exact
fatal-error TEXT is not a goal unless cheap" applies -- here it IS cheap, in
the sense that the templates are few and fully specified by the probe above,
but note the two number systems: `use 5.6` means v5.600.0 (hence the "did you
mean" hint), `use 5.006` means v5.6.0, and `use v5.6` means v5.6.0.  perl's
own rule: a bare number is a float version, `x.y.z` and `vX.Y.Z` are tuple
versions, and the failure is raised at BEGIN time ("BEGIN failed--compilation
aborted" follows every one of them), which is where PCL must raise it too for
an `eval "use ..."` to trap it.

The module half needs `$Module::VERSION` read AFTER the module is loaded and
compared with perl's version rules (a v-string `$VERSION` prints back as
`v35.36.0`, a string `'35.36'` as `35.36` -- use.t asserts both spellings).
subject: `use VERSION` / `no VERSION` / `use MODULE VERSION` never CHECK the version -- every requirement is silently satisfied; t/comp/use.t's 34 fail rows
